title: Room between the shirts
hook: Same five shirts, shorter rail. What happens to the space between them?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that the spaces between hanging clothes let damp air move away, so crowding items together slows each one down even though more of them fit

misconception: The same five shirts keep the same 5 cm gap on a shorter rail.
objective: Five shirts always take 40 cm of rail. Only the rail left over is shared out as gaps, so a shorter rail shrinks every gap, even with the same five shirts. At 0 cm, neighbours touch and no open path is left between them.

recall.question: A 52 cm rail holds 5 garments, each 8 cm wide, with equal gaps between them. How wide is each of the 4 gaps?
recall.why: Five garments use 5 × 8 = 40 cm, leaving 12 cm for 4 gaps: 3 cm each. Add more garments and the gaps close to zero, and the open air paths go with them. The diagram does not compute airflow.
